blocks.x: Today you will open a spreadsheet for the first time and learn its three building blocks: cells, rows and columns. By the end you will be able to type data into a sheet and tell a friend where each number lives.
Use the free Google Sheets on your phone or computer. You only need a Gmail account.

blocks.title: A beginner's tour of Google Sheets
blocks.searchQuery: Google Sheets beginner tutorial for first time users

blocks.x: A spreadsheet is a big grid. Each small box is a cell. A row runs left to right and has a number. A column runs up and down and has a letter. Every cell has an address made from its column and row, like B3.

Imagine a shop owner in Aba who writes the price of each item in a notebook. In a spreadsheet, the item names go in column A and the prices go in column B. Row 2 might hold 'Rice' in A2 and 45000 in B2.
Do not type the naira sign into number cells. Type 45000 and format the column as currency later.

blocks.title: Typing and formatting data in a sheet
blocks.searchQuery: Google Sheets enter data and format numbers beginner

blocks.x: Create a sheet with five items you bought this week and their prices. Put the names in column A and the prices in column B. Then write down the address of the most expensive item.

questions.q: Which is the address of the cell in column C, row 5?
